chapter_name: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
learning_objective:
Recall the definitions of the x-axis, y-axis, and origin in the Cartesian coordinate system.
Explain the sign conventions for measuring distances from the origin along the coordinate axes.
Apply sign conventions to determine the coordinates of a point given its direction and distance from the origin.
Explain the definition and coordinates of the origin.
Interpret the role of the origin as a reference point for coordinate measurements.
Apply the concept of origin to locate points in the coordinate plane.
Explain the condition for a point to lie on the x-axis or y-axis.
Apply the rule y=0 or x=0 to classify points on axes.
Analyze the relationship between the sign of coordinates and the direction from the origin.
Recall the four quadrants and their sign conventions.
Explain the sign conventions of coordinates in each quadrant.
Classify points into quadrants based on the signs of their coordinates.
Interpret the location of a point in the Cartesian plane based on its coordinate signs.
Analyze the coordinates of a point given its quadrant.
Describe the sign conventions for coordinates in all four quadrants.
Apply the sign rules to determine the quadrant of a point from its coordinates.
Classify a set of points into quadrants based on the signs of their coordinates.
Explain the meaning of the coordinates (x, y) as perpendicular distances from the axes.
Interpret the ordered pair (x, y) to determine the perpendicular distances of a point from the axes.
Explain the derivation of the distance formula using the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem.
Calculate the distance between two points using the distance formula.
Solve real-world problems involving distance in coordinate geometry.
Analyze geometric properties of shapes using distance calculations.
Explain the rule for reflection of a point across the y-axis.
Apply the reflection rule to determine the coordinates of reflected points.
Analyze whether reflection across the y-axis preserves distances between points.
Verify the properties of reflection by calculating side lengths using the distance formula.
State the midpoint formula and explain its derivation as the average of the x- and y-coordinates.
Apply the midpoint formula to compute the midpoint of a line segment given its endpoints or to find a missing endpoint given the midpoint and one endpoint.
Analyze given coordinate points to determine whether one is the midpoint of the segment formed by the other two and justify the conclusion.
